model.space: the standardized-anomaly field ml/rollout_spatial.py scores: per-pixel per-channel, de-climatologised against the TRAIN-year monthly climatology and z-scored, nan->0 at unobserved cells (StdMonths)
model.unobserved_cells: enter the covariance as 0, which is the value StdMonths hands every consumer of this space, the codec's own slab included
model.propagator: G(tau) = C(tau) C(0)^-1 in PC space
model.pairs_rule: consecutive axis rows whose BOTH bins are training bins, so no pair steps across a held-out year
model.reduction: PCA by the T x T Gram matrix (numpy eigh) — exact, no oversampling parameter; sklearn is not installed on the boxes
model.initial_condition: the TRUE standardized state at the start row, projected on the EOFs — the same row persistence is read from
model.channels_rule: observed at ANY start row — a strict superset of the channels `op = obs_target & obs_start` can ever be true on; the complement is ASSERTED to contribute zero at every scored step, and the run refuses if it does not

eigen.note: |lambda| < 1 for every mode means the forecast relaxes to the training mean (climatology in this standardized space) as the lead grows, which is what makes msss_clim approach 0 rather than diverge. A radius at or above 1 invalidates every long-lead row in this entry.

cadence.note: every `h` is an AXIS STEP, not a month. `horizon_auc` averages msss_clim over h=1..horizon_steps and is a function of THIS axis's lead sampling; `horizon_auc_daymatched` averages the twelve leads above and is the only one comparable with an archived corridor AUC.

inputs.doc: E-066 · LIM BASELINE — a Linear Inverse Model (Penland & Sardeshmukh) fitted on the standardised-anomaly field's own training bins (eight scoreable channels over the window's 86,698 ocean pixels; PCA to K = 50 / 100 / 200 modes; G(tau) = C(tau) C(0)^-1 at tau = one pentad, consecutive training pairs only) and rolled from #516's identical starts at the identical horizon (73 pentads, 3 starts per held-out year), scored through ml/rollout_spatial.py's own battery (msss_clim / msss_pers / msss_damped / acc / amp_ratio per lead, gate / corridor / window, per channel) so the paper can put a classical row beside the transformer heads' (#516 206.66M, #520 7.6M, #523 40.4M). Pre-registered reading: at every lead, does the head beat the LIM by more than the head's own reference spread? A head below the LIM at leads >= 2 makes the LIM the programme's reference model (REBOOT_PLAN step 6). No transport read-out here (field only). · params none (a fitted linear operator; nothing trains) · stage eval-only · data family4_na025_pentad_r2 · arch LIM K 50/100/200 over 86,698 px x 8 ch, tau 5 d · steps 197428 (= run-415's count, zero training) · resume run-415 (read for its args and channel names only).
